query:
INSERT INTO quickfireQuestions
  (type, question, reviewAnswer, echoCategory, category, difficulty, isActive, submissionStatus)
VALUES
('quickReview','What are the 5 views in the FAST exam?','RUQ (Morison pouch), LUQ (splenorenal), pelvic (pouch of Douglas/rectovesical), pericardial, and bilateral pleural','pocus','POCUS','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the normal IVC collapsibility index for low CVP?','>50% collapse with inspiration (sniff) = CVP <8 mmHg','pocus','POCUS','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the lung sliding sign?','Hyperechoic pleural line moving with respiration — confirms lung aeration','pocus','POCUS','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the seashore sign on M-mode lung ultrasound?','Sandy pattern below the pleural line — indicates normal lung sliding (air-filled lung)','pocus','POCUS','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the barcode sign on M-mode lung ultrasound?','Parallel horizontal lines — indicates absent lung sliding (pneumothorax or apnea)','pocus','POCUS','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What are B-lines on lung ultrasound?','Vertical hyperechoic artifacts arising from the pleural line — indicate interstitial fluid (pulmonary edema)','pocus','POCUS','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the threshold for pathologic B-lines?','≥3 B-lines in a single intercostal space','pocus','POCUS','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the lung point sign?','Transition point between absent and present lung sliding — pathognomonic for pneumothorax','pocus','POCUS','advanced',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the BLUE protocol?','Bedside Lung Ultrasound in Emergency — algorithm for acute respiratory failure using A-lines, B-lines, and pleural effusion patterns','pocus','POCUS','advanced',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the normal E-point septal separation (EPSS) on POCUS?','<7 mm (>10 mm suggests reduced LVEF)','pocus','POCUS','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the parasternal long axis (PLAX) view used for in cardiac POCUS?','LV size, pericardial effusion, aortic root, mitral valve motion, EPSS','pocus','POCUS','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the subxiphoid view used for in cardiac POCUS?','Pericardial effusion, RV/LV ratio, IVC size','pocus','POCUS','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the McConnell sign?','RV free wall hypokinesis with preserved apical motion — suggests acute pulmonary embolism','pocus','POCUS','advanced',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the D-sign in cardiac POCUS?','Flattened or D-shaped interventricular septum — indicates RV pressure or volume overload','pocus','POCUS','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the normal bladder volume threshold before catheterization?','>300–400 mL (urinary retention)','pocus','POCUS','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the formula for bladder volume on POCUS?','Length × Width × Height × 0.523 (prolate ellipsoid)','pocus','POCUS','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the RUSH exam?','Rapid Ultrasound in Shock and Hypotension — assesses pump, tank, and pipes','pocus','POCUS','advanced',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the normal gallbladder wall thickness on POCUS?','≤3 mm (fasting)','pocus','POCUS','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the piezoelectric effect?','Conversion of mechanical energy (pressure) to electrical energy — basis of ultrasound transducer function','physics','Physics','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the speed of sound in soft tissue?','1540 m/s (used as the assumed constant in clinical ultrasound)','physics','Physics','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the relationship between frequency and resolution vs penetration?','Higher frequency = better resolution, less penetration; lower frequency = worse resolution, better penetration','physics','Physics','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the axial resolution of an ultrasound beam?','Ability to distinguish two objects along the beam axis; determined by pulse length (spatial pulse length / 2)','physics','Physics','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the lateral resolution of an ultrasound beam?','Ability to distinguish two objects side by side; best at the focal zone','physics','Physics','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is acoustic impedance?','Density × speed of sound (Z = ρ × c); determines the amount of reflection at tissue interfaces','physics','Physics','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the Nyquist limit in Doppler ultrasound?','The maximum velocity that can be accurately measured without aliasing; equals PRF/2','physics','Physics','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is aliasing in pulsed wave Doppler?','Velocity exceeds the Nyquist limit — waveform wraps around and appears on the opposite side','physics','Physics','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the Doppler equation?','Δf = (2 × f₀ × v × cos θ) / c; where Δf = frequency shift, v = velocity, θ = angle of insonation','physics','Physics','advanced',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the optimal Doppler angle of insonation?','<60° (ideally <30°) — at 90° there is no Doppler shift','physics','Physics','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is posterior acoustic shadowing?','Reduction in echoes behind a highly reflective or attenuating structure (e.g., calculus, bone)','physics','Physics','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is posterior acoustic enhancement?','Increased echoes behind a fluid-filled structure — indicates low attenuation (e.g., cyst)','physics','Physics','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the ALARA principle?','As Low As Reasonably Achievable — minimize ultrasound exposure while maintaining diagnostic quality','physics','Physics','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What are the two main bioeffects of diagnostic ultrasound?','Thermal (heating) and mechanical (cavitation)','physics','Physics','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the mechanical index (MI)?','Measure of cavitation risk; MI = peak negative pressure / √frequency; <1.9 for diagnostic use','physics','Physics','advanced',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the thermal index (TI)?','Measure of tissue heating risk; TI = acoustic power / power required to raise tissue 1°C','physics','Physics','advanced',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is reverberation artifact?','Multiple parallel echoes from a highly reflective surface — creates false echoes behind the real structure','physics','Physics','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the comet-tail artifact?','Short, bright reverberation artifact — seen with small metallic objects or cholesterol crystals','physics','Physics','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the normal thyroid lobe size?','Length 4–6 cm, AP 1.5–2 cm, width 2–2.5 cm; isthmus ≤3 mm','thyroid','Thyroid','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the normal thyroid echogenicity?','Homogeneous, hyperechoic relative to surrounding strap muscles','thyroid','Thyroid','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the ACR TI-RADS classification?','Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System — 5-category risk stratification for thyroid nodules (TR1–TR5)','thyroid','Thyroid','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What nodule features increase TI-RADS score?','Solid composition, hypoechogenicity, irregular margins, microcalcifications, taller-than-wide shape','thyroid','Thyroid','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the sonographic appearance of a thyroid cyst?','Anechoic, thin-walled, posterior acoustic enhancement — TR1 (benign)','thyroid','Thyroid','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the sonographic appearance of papillary thyroid carcinoma?','Hypoechoic, solid, irregular margins, microcalcifications, taller-than-wide, intranodular vascularity','thyroid','Thyroid','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the ACR TI-RADS FNA threshold for TR5 nodules?','≥1 cm (FNA recommended)','thyroid','Thyroid','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the ACR TI-RADS FNA threshold for TR4 nodules?','≥1.5 cm (FNA recommended)','thyroid','Thyroid','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is Hashimoto thyroiditis on ultrasound?','Heterogeneous, hypoechoic thyroid with fibrous bands, increased vascularity, and pseudonodules','thyroid','Thyroid','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is Graves disease on ultrasound?','Diffusely enlarged, hypoechoic thyroid with markedly increased vascularity (thyroid inferno)','thyroid','Thyroid','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the thyroid inferno sign?','Markedly increased Doppler vascularity throughout the thyroid — classic for Graves disease','thyroid','Thyroid','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the sonographic appearance of a colloid cyst?','Anechoic with echogenic foci (comet-tail artifacts) — benign colloid nodule','thyroid','Thyroid','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the normal parathyroid gland size?','<5 mm (not usually visible on ultrasound unless enlarged)','thyroid','Thyroid','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the sonographic appearance of a parathyroid adenoma?','Hypoechoic, oval, posterior to the thyroid lobe, with a feeding vessel','thyroid','Thyroid','intermediate',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the normal thyroid volume?','Male: <25 mL; Female: <18 mL','thyroid','Thyroid','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the ACR TI-RADS score for a purely cystic nodule?','TR1 (0 points) — benign, no FNA needed','thyroid','Thyroid','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the ACR TI-RADS score for a spongiform nodule?','TR2 (0 points) — benign, no FNA needed','thyroid','Thyroid','beginner',1,'draft'),
('quickReview','What is the taller-than-wide criterion in thyroid nodule assessment?','AP diameter > transverse diameter on transverse view — associated with malignancy','thyroid','Thyroid','intermediate',1,'draft')
